input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Two material gaps against the fallback. (1) Exit charge: Section 4.2(a) (p0026) imposes on the Company alone a Termination Payment of half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, payable in eight quarterly instalments (p0029) with no reciprocal HDI payment (p0028). Against Section 3.1 fees (30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month) that is roughly $600,000 on $2,000,000 of Net Sales versus about $140,000 of three months' fees — far above the fallback cap. Operation 2 therefore imposes a three-month fee ceiling as a "lesser of" on the existing calculation, so the Company still owes nothing where trailing Net Sales are $800,000 or less and Section 4.2(b)'s zero-or-less netting remains operative. (2) Section 4.1 (p0024) is symmetric ("terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice") with no words confining HDI to the expiry of the then-current term, and the "Such notice shall specify the date" sentence would let HDI pick any date 90+ days out; the asymmetry cannot be read into those words. Operation 1 states the split expressly: the Company may terminate on ninety (90) days' written notice at any time, HDI only effective at the expiration of the then-current term, with the 90-day notice retained for both. The remaining point — that 4.2(a) still bites on a termination for HDI's breach — is outside this checklist, so it is raised in the comment rather than drafted in. Preferred (30 days, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees) is not pursued: no prepaid fees exist under this revenue-share fee model.

proposal.summary: Make the Company's 90-day convenience right express, limit HDI's Section 4.1 termination to the end of the then-current term, and cap the Termination Payment at three months of Section 3.1 fees via a lesser-of ceiling on the existing calculation.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 4.1 now states expressly that we may terminate on ninety (90) days' written notice at any time while HDI may terminate only effective at the expiration of the then-current term; the symmetric wording did not carry that split. In Section 4.2(a) we have capped the Termination Payment at three months of Section 3.1 fees as a ceiling on the existing calculation, so the netting outcome in Section 4.2(b) is preserved. We would also expect 4.2(a) not to bite where we terminate for HDI's breach, consistent with Section 1.6.

ops.oldText: on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other.
ops.newText: on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated upon ninety (90) days written notice by the Company at any time or by HDI only effective at the expiration of the then-current term.

ops.oldText: the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
ops.newText: the amount of which shall be the lesser of (i) the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, divided by two, and (ii) the payments due to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.

Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
